raw_draft.postverify_tldr: CBOT soybeans sit on a genuinely two-sided board: the US balance sheet is the tight leg -- the stocks-to-use ratio for 2026/27 reads 10.72% of domestic use [N128], the 23rd percentile of its own record [N130] and falling three marketing years running, with the board crush margin at 2.43 USD/bu [N164] still pulling beans through the crush -- while the loose leg is the tropical Pacific, where the sea-surface anomaly is +1.8 degC in July 2026 [N20], the 93rd percentile of its own record [N22], a warm phase the driver model signs against soybean price at medium confidence over one to two quarters. On the three-month horizon the chain from Brent crude into CBOT soybeans is the one the record speaks to, and only two of the eight past times Brent sat this far out carry a price reading over that band -- too thin a sample for a middle figure, so I give you the mechanism and no range.
raw_draft.postverify_mechanism:
## Mechanism

**Where the balance sits.** Two loud readings lean opposite ways and I will name both. The tight leg is physical: the US stocks-to-use ratio at 10.72% [N128] is past the line the desk calls tight and has fallen three marketing years in a row, and a thin buffer is what makes any supply shock convex to the upside rather than linear -- the same thin buffer caps the downside from a big crop. Against it, the warm-phase Pacific reading at +1.8 degC [N20] is declared to move soybeans the opposite way, and that effect window opens around February 2026 and closes around January 2027, so the three months asked about sit inside it. My lean: the tight-buffer leg dominates the next quarter, because the stocks-to-use link is high confidence and near-term, while the Pacific link is medium confidence and works only through a South American crop still ahead of us. That is a model ranking, not a measured attribution. One caution on the crowd -- managed money is at 241,501 contracts [N50], the 99th percentile of its own record [N52] and already easing over the last week; that reading amplifies a move rather than cushioning it, and it is what funds held, not a cause.

**The evidence, dated.** The stocks-to-use figure and the Argentine, Brazilian and Chinese balance rows were known 11 September 2026. The Pacific anomaly is a July 2026 reading, rising in each of the last eight months. The crush margin at 2.43 USD/bu [N164] is a 23 September 2026 print, the 89th percentile of its own record [N166], having peaked at the 96th in July 2026 [N170]. Brazilian exports at 118 MMT for 2026/27 [N59] sit at the 99th percentile of their own record [N61] -- a large competing origin, and the reason the US export channel is the soft spot. US export shipments ran 775.39 thousand MT in the week to 17 September 2026 [N196], rising three weeks after bottoming at the 3rd percentile in August 2026 [N199]. The November 2026 delivery settled at 1317.5 US cents/bushel on 24 September 2026 [N201], up 176 over sixty-three sessions [N205]. Where the record is thin: the Pacific reading has two comparable past states and neither carries a price outcome over the band -- what moved was the anomaly itself, +0.18 degC to the lag open and -0.04 degC to its close from the February 2025 state [N225][N226], and -1.07 degC then -1.78 degC from the January 2024 state [N227][N228]; the corpus holds no dated document explaining either. That is history, not a forecast. The numbers behind this page were known through 25 September 2026, the oldest reaching back to April 2011; the newest dated document is 9 April 2026; the price tape runs through 24 September 2026.

**The chain into the next quarter.** Brent crude against its own five-year record reads 0.51 z in August 2026 [N177], the 68th percentile [N179] after peaking at the 98th in April 2026 [N180]; the model expects it to lift the crush margin, and the readings agree. The crush margin at the 89th percentile [N169] is expected to pull the stocks-to-use ratio down, and the readings agree. The stocks-to-use ratio at the 23rd percentile [N130] is expected to move the calendar spread the other way -- the readings do not settle it -- and the calendar spread, for which no series is served here, is expected to lift the soybean price over zero to one quarter. So the chain is directionally intact for three links and goes dark at the last one. The dated report at the first link is from 1 September 2005 [E14], outside the lag the model allows, so treat that link as mechanism. The history: of the past times Brent sat this far out, eight had a crush-margin reading, which moved the model's way in five and against it in three; eight further times no reading published inside the lag. Two other chains reach markets this question did not name -- one from rising biodiesel mandates, documented 18 March 2026 [E11], and one from Chinese tariffs through export shipments -- and both stop at the same dark final link. Two hundred ninety-nine chains run into these markets in all. Counting a shared Pacific reading once, not once per path.

## The record

The settled USDA season-average farm price rose from $9.59/bu [N236] in MY2009/10 to $11.30/bu [N237] in MY2010/11 -- a survey-based figure, not a futures settle. On the same clock, the Pacific anomaly measured -0.68 degC over January–April 2011 [N238] against +1.8 degC now [N239], and the driest US growing cell read 0.9 z in April 2011 [N240] against 0.92 z in August 2026 [N241]; the 2011 cool phase is documented as cutting Paraná yields by more than 30 percent [E12], reported 1 September 2012.

Coincidence readings over the October 2023–April 2024 episode window, which ended 8 April 2024, two years before this as-of. CBOT soybeans fell -9.95 % [N242] on the May 2024 delivery.
- **Soybeans and ZCE rapeseed meal** -- the model records them competing for the same demand, so tight soybean supply should pull rapeseed meal higher; rapeseed meal moved -6.37 % [N243] in yuan while soybeans moved in dollars; the read: the relation held over that window, in-sample only, with the currency move inside the comparison. The yuan per dollar rate moved -0.91 % over the same window [N244].
- **Soybeans and ZCE rapeseed oil** -- same declared competition; rapeseed oil moved -3.9 % [N245] in yuan; the read: the relation held over that window.
- **Soybeans and CBOT soybean meal** -- joined by the same crush; meal moved -10.02 % [N246]; the read: the relation held.
- **Soybean meal and soybean oil** -- declared to compete for the same demand; soyoil moved -8.11 % [N247]; the read: the two moves sat at odds with the declared relation over that window.
- **Soybean oil and CME palm oil** -- declared substitutes; palm moved +14.84 % [N248]; the read: the two moves sat at odds with the declared relation over that window. That is the finding, stated as it stands.

MATIF rapeseed cannot be read here: the window predates that market's own price history.

## Where the record disagrees

Within the same episode window above, the record forks: the soybean-to-meal and soybean-to-rapeseed legs held, while the meal-to-oil and oil-to-palm legs sat at odds with what the model declares. Do not smooth those into one story.

## What to watch

- **The US stocks-to-use ratio**, 10.72% [N128], known 11 September 2026, past the line the desk calls tight at the 25th percentile. This reads wrong if the next print turns back inside that line or the three-year falling run breaks. Its next print is a restatement of a period that cannot turn inside three months, so read it as standing context; the reading that can turn inside the horizon is the crush margin, which prints every session.
- **The tropical Pacific anomaly**, +1.8 degC [N20], July 2026, past the line the desk calls strong at one and a half degC, rising eight months running. This reads wrong if the next print turns back inside that line or the run breaks. Conditionally, the declared lag window counted from that reading opens 2026-10-31 and closes 2027-01-31.
- **China's soybean carry-in stocks**, 44.36 MMT [N62], known 11 September 2026, the 98th percentile of its own record [N64] and one of the conditions of the price-pressuring trade-war demand-loss pattern. This reads wrong if the next print returns it to the middle of its own record.

Three items cleared the bar on this market; the rest of the nominated list sat on corn and rapeseed meal and I have left it there.
